read between the lines and get behind the story to try to answer these questions and that frequently involves
imagining what's going on within these stories what the terrain of a battle might be like or what the opponent's
Weaponry or uniforms might be like or what might be going through someone's mind or or what cultural mores are
governing their behavior but one thing that all these attempts to read between the lines pre suppose is that these
stories are historical and that there was an enemy or there was somebody who
had something going through their mind but many of these stories are not historical and even the ones that are based on historical events are still
being told by authors later on authors who are skilled in telling stories and
so rather than trying to imagine what historical might be going on Behind these stories better question might be
why is the author telling the story this way and what is the author hoping to accomplish by telling the story this way
